record_identity.title: Moltbook database exposure revealed private communications and API authentication tokens

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Moltbook database exposure revealed private communications and API authentication tokens
incident_identity.date_basis: Wiz’s UTC timeline records initial contact on January 31 and iterative fixes through February 1. February 2 is publication, not the disclosure or exposure-start date; the earlier beginning of exposure is unknown.

summary: Wiz researchers found that Moltbook’s public database connection lacked row-level security. They reported access to about 35,000 email addresses, 4,060 private conversations and approximately 1.5 million authentication tokens. Some messages held third-party credentials. The tokens could permit agent impersonation; that possible misuse was separate from the researchers’ database access. Wiz contacted the maintainer on 31 January 2026. Initial fixes restricted sensitive reads, but researchers could still change a live post. Further fixes blocked writes and secured newly discovered tables by 01:00 UTC on 1 February. Wiz said it could no longer revert its test post after write access was blocked; the team later deleted the post. Wiz also reported deleting the data accessed during research and verification.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The originating Wiz account identifies a public Supabase connection and missing row-level security, rather than treating an intentionally public connection key alone as the defect. Its queries reached agent credentials, private communications and email tables. Business Insider’s under-three-minute claim remains attributed reporting. Wiz distinguishes credential-enabled impersonation from its demonstrated unauthenticated modification of an existing public post. Its UTC timeline separates January 31 disclosure, partial read restrictions, a remaining write pathway, write restriction, discovery of additional tables and final reported remediation on February 1. The researcher could not undo the test edit after write restriction and reports later maintainer deletion and deletion of research copies. No inspected account establishes malicious token reuse, downstream prompt execution or all prior third-party access.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Missing database restrictions exposed private information and credentials. Researchers also demonstrated a live integrity effect after the first repair. Iterative fixes and the blocked attempt to revert the post support bounded remediation verification. They do not prove that prior access was fully discovered or that all copied information was recovered. The record does not establish an AI or governance process using technical reachability as an authority basis. The renewed disclosure reached the maintainer and produced an observable restriction on the tested write pathway. That bounded control effect is distinct from the earlier exposure and from full-platform assurance. The bounded response finding does not classify the whole occurrence as Aligned. Moltbook exposed private communications and email records and permitted a demonstrated unauthenticated post edit. The public connection identifier is not the secret or defect. Distinct read and write operations crossed private-content and owner-edit boundaries; later repair does not erase those operations. Moltbook’s database returned agent authentication tokens and private messages containing third-party API secrets. These secret objects left authorised custody. The public Supabase connection identifier is excluded, and possible impersonation is not represented as an observed takeover. Wiz could no longer revert its live test edit after unauthenticated writes were restricted. This is a concrete test of the post-edit boundary. The Aligned result covers that route and time; it does not certify all tables or recover prior copies.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that AI-agent platforms remain dependent on conventional application-security controls for credentials, private communications and account integrity.
assessment_boundaries: The disclosed start of researcher contact is known; the start and full duration of the exposure are not.
Credential-enabled impersonation and prompt injection were capabilities, not demonstrated downstream attacks in the inspected account. The researcher’s test post modification was realised.
Founder and researcher descriptions of AI-assisted development do not identify the actor responsible for the missing database policy.
Reported fixes and deletion do not establish recovery of all possible third-party copies.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Preserve a source-specific paraphrase that links the primary occurrence evidence to VIGIL's governance interpretation without treating taxonomy classification as source fact.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Wiz found a public Supabase connection in client code and missing row-level security, enabling database reads and writes. Business Insider reported access in under three minutes.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A client-visible connection key is not itself the security defect; backend policy determines its permitted effects.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The public connection and tokens established capability. The account does not show an AI or governance process using that reachability as its permission basis. A vulnerability alone is excluded from this authority-inference class.

The missing backend policies were tested through queries that returned private records and secret tokens, detailed in the following episodes. The connection identifier was intentionally public; the demonstrated private-record retrieval establishes the information boundary crossing.

clauses.adjudication_note: The missing backend policies were tested through queries that returned private records and secret tokens, detailed in the following episodes. The connection identifier was intentionally public; the demonstrated private-record retrieval establishes the information boundary crossing.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The accessible database contained about 35,000 email addresses and 4,060 private conversations, some with third-party credentials.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Actual confidential-information exposure differs from subsequent use of that information.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Private messages and email records were returned outside their intended private audience. This is demonstrated confidential-content exposure, independently of later use.
Some exposed private messages contained third-party API secrets. Their retrieval crossed the custody boundary even without a subsequent API call.

clauses.adjudication_note: Private messages and email records were returned outside their intended private audience. This is demonstrated confidential-content exposure, independently of later use.

clauses.source_paraphrase: About 1.5 million agent authentication tokens were exposed, creating impersonation capability.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Credential reachability does not establish realised account takeover.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Agent authentication tokens were returned through an unauthenticated database route. These were secret account credentials, unlike the intentionally public Supabase connection identifier.

clauses.adjudication_note: Agent authentication tokens were returned through an unauthenticated database route. These were secret account credentials, unlike the intentionally public Supabase connection identifier.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Wiz contacted the maintainer on January 31 at 21:48 UTC and reported the row-level security issue at 22:06.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Research access and coordinated disclosure are separate actions.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Wiz sent the row-level security report to the maintainer. The recorded replies and table restrictions trace this signal to the responsible operator and a bounded response; the initial report did not close the later-discovered write and table exposures.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At 23:29 UTC the first group of tables was secured; at 00:13 on February 1 further private tables were secured.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Partial remediation must retain its limited scope.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The maintainer secured named groups of sensitive tables in response to the disclosure. The timeline records these limited dispositions rather than treating the first repair as closure of every exposed route.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At 00:31 Wiz discovered remaining write access and demonstrated a change to a live post after sensitive reads had been restricted.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A realised integrity test is distinct from hypothetical credential misuse and from read exposure.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Wiz changed an existing live post through an unauthenticated write route. Public readability did not authorise an unrelated caller to edit that post.

clauses.adjudication_note: Wiz changed an existing live post through an unauthenticated write route. Public readability did not authorise an unrelated caller to edit that post.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Wiz notified the team again; at 00:44 write access was blocked. The researcher could no longer revert the post.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The blocked reversal is direct reported verification of this write boundary, not proof that every endpoint was secured.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Renewed notification of the remaining write route reached the maintainer and produced a write restriction. Wiz’s blocked reversal connects this escalation with a bounded corrective effect.

After the maintainer restricted unauthenticated writes, Wiz could no longer revert the test post. The attempted write exercised the activated restriction and demonstrated its protective effect on that pathway. Other tables and prior copies remain outside this finding.
After write restrictions changed, Wiz’s attempted reversal of its post edit was blocked. That concrete write attempt demonstrated enforcement on the tested post route only.

clauses.source_paraphrase: At 00:50 researchers discovered further exposed tables; Wiz’s timeline records the final fix at 01:00.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Successive discoveries show why earlier fixes must not be represented as complete remediation.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Further private tables remained exposed after the earlier limited repairs. Those later-discovered records were outside the protection achieved on the already restricted routes.

clauses.adjudication_note: Further private tables remained exposed after the earlier limited repairs. Those later-discovered records were outside the protection achieved on the already restricted routes.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The team deleted the test content hours later; Wiz reports deleting data accessed during research and fix verification.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Later cleanup and reported research-data deletion differ from restricting future access. Their exact ordering relative to every fix is not established.
clauses.adjudication_note: Deletion of test content and reported research-data cleanup limit the aftermath. They do not establish recovery of every copy or independently demonstrate a new protective-control pathway.
